newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: BWT says new product to boost 1998 revenue.
newsitem.headline: BWT says new product to boost 1998 revenue.

text.p: Austria's BWT AG, Europe's leading manufacturer of water treatment technology, said on Friday that a new product should generate sales of around 200 million schillings and earnings of some 56 million schillings in 1998.
BWT chairman Andreas Weissenbacher told reporters that the machine, dubbed "AQA total", was expected to bring in the group extra revenue of 700 million schillings in 2001.
The product prevents the build-up of lime without the use of chemicals and salt and thereby offers sustained protection to the environment.
Weissenbacher declined to give exact figures for the cost of development, but said more than 60 million schillings would be invested in 1997 for bringing the product onto the market.
Around two thirds of that would be allocated for marketing, with the remainder going into production.
Some 15,000 machines were due to be produced this year.
Production is expected to increase to 100,000 units a year within the next three years, Weissenbacher said.
AQA total is being developed as a mass product for the prevention of lime formation in domestic water consumption but could also be modified for further applications, he added.
